name: Judas Iscariot
summary: One of the twelve apostles, the son of Simon, who kept the disciples' money bag. He betrayed Jesus to the chief priests for thirty pieces of silver.

key_moments.title: Complains About the Costly Ointment
key_moments.description: When Mary poured costly ointment on Jesus' feet, Judas asked why it was not sold and given to the poor. He said this not because he cared for the poor, but because he was a thief who kept the bag.

key_moments.title: Agrees to Betray Jesus for Silver
key_moments.description: Judas went to the chief priests and asked what they would give him to hand Jesus over. They agreed on thirty pieces of silver, and from then on he looked for a chance to betray Him.

key_moments.title: Takes the Bread and Goes Out
key_moments.description: At supper Jesus said one of them would betray Him, and He gave a piece of bread to Judas. Then Satan entered Judas, and he went out into the night.

key_moments.title: Betrays Jesus with a Kiss
key_moments.description: Judas came with a great crowd carrying swords and clubs from the chief priests. He had told them the one he kissed was the man, so he greeted Jesus and kissed Him, and they took Jesus.

key_moments.title: Throws Down the Silver and Hangs Himself
key_moments.description: When Judas saw that Jesus was condemned, he regretted it and brought back the silver, saying he had betrayed innocent blood. He threw it down in the temple and went and hanged himself.
